info.name: Fonja API
info.description: Ordered QA run for the Fonja backend. Run folders top to bottom — each captures ids into the environment for the next. Import fonja.postman_environment.json alongside and set baseUrl, token, adminToken, integrationKey.

item.name: 1 · Health & sign-in
item.description: Get a JWT by opening {{baseUrl}}/oauth2/authorization/google in a browser and copying responseData.accessToken into the `token` environment variable. There is no password login.

item.name: 5 · Admin bootstrap
item.description: No API grants ADMIN. Run:  INSERT INTO user_roles (user_id, role) VALUES ({{userId}}, 'ADMIN');  then sign in again and put the new accessToken in `adminToken`.

request.description: Use Send and Download. Not wrapped in the JSON envelope.
Skip on the happy path — a rejected request cannot be approved afterwards.
Sends the campaign back to DRAFT with rejectionReason. Re-run Launch afterwards.

item.name: 6b · Public feed (no token)
item.description: Runs after the campaign is approved in 6. Every request here is anonymous on purpose: the feed and a campaign page are the two reads a visitor gets before signing up.

exec: pm.test("cards carry creatorName and raisedAmount", () => { const c = d.content[0]; pm.expect(c.creatorName).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(c).to.have.property("raisedAmount"); pm.expect(c).to.have.property("donationCount"); });
pm.test("descending by raisedAmount", () => { for (let i = 1; i < c.length; i++) pm.expect(c[i-1].raisedAmount).to.be.at.least(c[i].raisedAmount); });

item.name: Feed, filtered by category and search

exec: pm.test("400 with the accepted values", () => { pm.response.to.have.status(400); pm.expect(pm.response.json().responseMessage).to.include("NEWEST"); });
